Testimony of Rep. Allison Hepler presenting
LD 2027, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Woolwich the Woolwich
Veterans Memorial Bridge
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Good morning, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and members of the Transportation
Committee. I am Allison Hepler and I represent the towns of Arrowsic, Georgetown,
Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich. I am here today to present LD 2027, Resolve, to
Rename a Bridge in Woolwich the Woolwich Veterans Memorial Bridge.
If you traveled on Route l through Woolwich at any time in the last four years, you would be
familiar with what we now call the "Station 46" bridge, crossing the railroad tracks about 15 to
35 feet above grade just north of the Taste of Maine Restaurant. If you're a resident of Woolwich, you're very familiar with it. Update: It's finished, Maine Department of Transportation and Woolwich contractor Reed and Reed did a fantastic job, finishing early and working through the challenging January 2024 storms.
LD 2027 references "Bridge 3039 on Main Street in the Town of Woolwich," which was built in 1933. Prior to that, Route l crossed the railroad tracks at grade. According to MDOT, the Annual
Average Daily Traffic on the bridge in 2019 was nearly 19,000 vehicles. Many people cross this bridge, so it seems an appropriate venue to recognize the men and women from Woolwich who
have served our nation.
Woolwich honors its veterans in many ways. The Town hosts an annual Veterans Day Service in our historic Nequasset Meetinghouse every year on November 1 1. The Town also participates in a townwide Memorial Day commemoration. One of our local cemeteries, Laurel Grove, raised a monument to remember veterans who served in American wars. On Route 1 near the Sagadahoc Bridge, the Town dedicated Tanner Square in 1950, which contains a monument to the men and women who "served in World War II. It was named for Woolwich resident Pfc. Richard Tanner, a
paratrooper killed in action in France on July 4, 1944.
In addition, our community is very fortunate to have two veterans organizations, the SmithTobey American Legion Post 21 in Bath, and the Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 7738 based in Phippsburg. Both organizations and their members are active in the community, from hosting local suppers and providing space for local scouting troop meetings to sponsoring an annual
Toys for Tots campaign. The mission of Smith-Tobey is, "To help fellow veterans navigate the

. District 49: Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich

challenges of life after service, to advocate for their rights, and to ensure that the sacrifices of our
fallen heroes are never forgotten." Individual members are also involved with Honor Flight Maine. Woolwich Korean War veteran Bob Meade is a one-man committee dedicated to ensuring the care of Tanner Square. Their actions and involvement matter. The idea for this bridge renaming comes from a constituent and it has the unanimous support of
the Woolwich Selectboard. Names matter. I'm honored to advocate for this change and this recognition. Thanks for your time and I'm happy to answer any questions you have.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither for Nor Against LD 2027
Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Woolwich the Woolwich Veterans Memorial
Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 2027.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 3039.
Thank you.
